## Workshop schedule 


**Thursday 19th November, 2026**

| Approx time      | Item                                              |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| 09:30 - 09:50    |  [An overview of RNA-seq data analysis workflows](background.qmd)   |
| 09:50 - 10:30    | [Sequence Quality](sequence-quality.qmd)  |
| 10:30 - 10:50    | BREAK                                             |
| 10:50 - 12:15    | [Index, align and quantifying gene expression](index-align-quantify.qmd)          |
| 12:15 - 13:00    | LUNCH                                             |
| 13:00 - 13:30    | RNA-seq presentation by Dr Stephanie Waller           |
| 13:30 - 14:30    | [Identifying differentially expressed genes](dge.qmd)          |
| 14:30 - 14:50    | BREAK                                             |
| 14:50 - 16:00       | [Functional analysis](functional-analysis.qmd)               |
| 16:30            |  END OF DAY                                       |





## What's covered in this workshop

- Full RNAseq workflow of a New Zealand endemic species using both bash and R tools.  
- Illumina short-read quality assessment and pre-processing.  
- Aligning paired-end reads to a publically available genome.  
- Identifying differentially expressed genes with DEseq2. 
- Functional annotation using GOseq to investigate trends in expression.    

## What's not covered in this workshop

- Submitting and optimising HPC scheduled jobs (see Bash scripting and HPC Job Scheduler workshop)
- Extensive data manipulation and plotting in R, beyond the basics.  


## Setup

During the workshop, code will be run in real-time to demonstrate the analysis. This will be run on the REANNZ OpenOnDemand HPC platform which already has all the required software and R packages installed. 


## Attribution notice

This workshop is based on an existing [Genomics Aotearoa RNAseq workshop](https://genomicsaotearoa.github.io/RNA-seq-data-analysis-workflow-NZ/), shortened to fit in one day. Further attribution context is described in that workshop.
